_README: Metadata for every document in the Waswa knowledge corpus. Ingestion reads
only what is listed here: a markdown file with no manifest entry is skipped
and named in the output. That is deliberate. Authority level decides how
much weight an answer carries and whether it may be quoted to a customer at
all, and it cannot be inferred from a filename.
authority_level, per migration 035:
1  Approved product and rate data      (confirmed)
2  Approved company procedure          (proposed)
3  Approved strategy and scope         (proposed)
4  Specification and user stories      (proposed)
5  Internal working material           (proposed, not quotable)
6  Unverified                          (proposed, not quotable)
The levels assigned below are a proposal from reading each document, not a
business decision. Review them before setting review_status to approved.
DELIBERATELY LEFT OUT, and why — so nobody adds them by default later:
Navas_IoT_Unit_Cost_v26.06.12 and COMMISSION_POLICY_3DS-QSP-16.
Both hold money figures. Waswa's prompt refuses every pricing question,
and text that retrieval can reach works against that. Excluded entirely
rather than stored at a non-quotable level, so no later reclassification
can expose them.
NAVAS_CATALOG_v26.03.30.xlsx. Structured product data, not prose. It
belongs in abi_products_manager via the PPMM loader, where the product
tools can use it — flattened into chunks it retrieves badly and competes
with the level 1 tables.
telematics_platform_feature_framework_v26.03.31. Same reason: a matrix,
destined for abi_product_capabilities, not for the chunk corpus.
.NAVAS_USER_STORIES_v26.03.26 (the 11,531-row master backlog). Three
reasons. It says of itself that its rows are 'synthesized' and that its
billing, RBAC, compliance and retention logic is 'blueprint-level' and
not yet finalised — so it is machine-generated planning, not approved
specification. It is an engineering backlog (API, Kafka topic,
persistence design per row), which is not what a customer question is
about. And it does not fix the missing UKO stories: of its 1,033 'UKO'
mentions, 965 are the source-filename column repeating
'.UKO_USER_STORIES_26.03.09' — the mislabelled OLIWA file — so it
inherits the error one layer further removed.
STILL MISSING: genuine UKO user stories. No file found in Drive or on
disk contains them — everything so named is the OLIWA document.

documents.title: Sales Procedures 3DS-QMS-PR-09 ver26 (Uganda & Kenya)
documents.notes: The approval ladder Waswa routes proposals through (§26.6), the PFI workflow, and the ethical standards. NOTE: the numeric discount threshold is STILL not stated in ver26 — §26.6 says 'up to approved threshold' and 'above threshold' without a figure. The three percentages that do appear are something else: '>10% without approval' is a financial early-warning indicator (§15.2.6), '<5% discount misuse' and 'discount usage <10% of deals' are KPIs. The operative rule that IS stated: no discount without SMU/KCM approval, recorded in Odoo.

documents.title: Customer Journey Maps — Onboarding, Offboarding and After-Sales
documents.notes: Five sheets, transposed column-wise by scripts/xlsx_to_knowledge_md.py so each chunk is one journey step with its actions, questions, happy moments, pain points and opportunities together. Covers onboarding (25 steps), churn/offboarding (25) and after-sales fault handling (10), plus two responsibility matrices mapping actions to departments and ISO work instructions. TWO CAVEATS. It is dated January 2024, so it predates the v26 ecosystem rewrite and describes the customer process as it was then — where it disagrees with the vision scope document, the vision scope is newer. And it is mixed authority: the responsibility matrices are procedural (they cite ISO doc numbers) while the journey maps are descriptive, so the whole document takes the lower of the two levels.

documents.title: NAVAS CMS User Manual
documents.notes: How the CMS actually works, written for the people who use it — the only operational reference in the corpus, as opposed to specifications of what is designed. REDACTED ON INGEST: 9 currency amounts, via gdoc_to_knowledge_md.py --redact-currency. Eight were example time-token values in §7.6.1 (PIKI/OLIWA/UKO day rates for UG and KE); one was an example HIC threshold in the AI allocation section. Each is replaced in the markdown by '[amount withheld: pricing]', so the redaction is visible in git and in the chunk rather than silent. Everything else is verbatim.

documents.title: NAVAS Token Billing Strategy ver26.01.26a
documents.notes: The token model as a backlog of user stories: what a token is, token classes and their billing units (hour/event/km/MB/inference), and §'Billing Units != Tokens'. Directly relevant to the balance answers Waswa already gives, and the source for why a unit must never be reported as an hour. REDACTED ON INGEST: 3 currency amounts, same mechanism as the CMS manual. Note it is a backlog, so it describes intent and sequencing, not what is built.

documents.title: NAVAS Ecosystem Vision Scope Document
documents.notes: Supersedes NAVAS_VISION_SCOPE_DOC_v24.12.17. Plain-text export: no bold, no size variation, so headings come from ALL-CAPS section titles only. Two byte-identical copies were in the source folder; one was ingested.

documents.title: OLIWA User Stories
documents.notes: The file named UKO_USER_STORIES_26.03.09.pdf is byte-identical to this one and mentions OLIWA 61 times and UKO never. It is a mislabelled copy, not the UKO stories. The UKO user stories are missing from the corpus.

documents.title: CMS User Stories
documents.notes: Management-side stories. Describes what the CMS is specified to do, not what is built.

documents.title: Marketplace User Stories
documents.notes: Exported as a flattened spreadsheet (one page, 6pt, no ruling lines). Converted with --record-pattern so each app/story row is its own chunk. Rows carry app_code, app_name, theme and segment.

documents.title: UKO Dashboard KPI Framework
documents.notes: 32 modules, 6 dashboard cards each, three mini-KPIs per card. Defines KPI names and what they measure; it is not a statement that any of them is live.

documents.title: Navas Waswa AI Strategy
documents.notes: What Waswa is for. Useful to Waswa for answering questions about itself.

documents.title: 3D AI Agent Back-Office Automation Strategy
documents.notes: Internal operating plan, including staffing and cost intent. Level 5 is not quotable to a customer: Waswa may use it to understand a question, not to answer one.
